w: In the evening Swamishri travelled the nearby village of Dabhaasi and performed pujan of the installed murtis of Thakorji at the Swaminarayan mandir. After the shanti-paath Swamishri performed arti and blessed the assembly.

The chief editor of The Times of India, Mumbai, Shri Balkrishnan, praised Swamishri's socio-spiritual achievements and said that he is a spiritual engineer. Swamishri replied, "I have done nothing. Whatever is achieved is through God's grace and through the efforts of these sadhus and devotees."

Shri Balkrishnan responded, "But it is through your leadership that things are accomplished. I feel that Pramukh Swami should be given the Bharat Ratna award. Though you are the jewel of Bharat, there should be an official recognition by giving you the award."

Swamishri, pointing to a murti of Akshar and Purushottam, happily replied, "Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Yogiji Maharaj have given me the award. I am happy and contented with that. There is no need of worldly awards."
Despite all his grand achievements Swamishri has no desires for recognition because he is content with the blessings of God and his guru.
At 11.00 a.m. Swamishri visited the newly established sanskardham in Naroda, Amdavad, and performed pujan and arti.
At 5.00 p.m. Swamishri departed from Amdavad and arrived in Traj at 6.00 p.m. Swamishri performed arti and pujan of the murtis in the newly established hari mandir and blessed the devotees.
At 7.30 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Vadadala and performed arti and pujan of the deities at the newly built hari mandir.
At 8.15 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Bochasan.
Bal - Balika National Convention On the final full day of the National Bal-Balika Convention, balaks played two games with Swamishri – one nonverbal and the other verbal.

In the nonverbal game, ‘Vartan Vãto Karshe,’ Swamishri served as a judge for a game of charades played by sadhus and balaks. In the interactive verbal game, balaks took turns asking Swamishri various questions. Swamishri patiently answered all questions in detail, describing to balaks what they should learn by heart, narrating a parable of Yogiji Maharaj and describing how he became a sadhu. In the evening assembly, balaks and balikas observed Guru Purnima, in which they offered their thanks to Swamishri for being the ideal guru.

Balaks and balikas got a glimpse at some ideal disciples, such as Aruni, Eklavya, and Satyakam Jabali through dramas. Then, Swamishri demonstrated the extent of his guru bhakti towards Shastriji Maharaj by narrating an incident about this, as well as by singing ‘Shastriji Maharajno sang...’ Finally, several balaks were recognised for their commitment to niyam-dharma. Swamishri also played a game in which he guided a blindfolded balak through an obstacle course, demonstrating the necessity to put total faith in the words of the guru. Finally, after arti and mantra pushpanjali, Swamishri sprayed coloured water on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Thereafter, the balaks, one by one, were sprayed with the sanctified water.

The festival of Guru Purnima is celebrated every year in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Bochasan. Today the assembly was addressed by senior sadhus who extolled the glory of Shriji Maharaj and the Guru Parampara. The programme was interlaced with kirtans and a traditional dance. Swamishri arrived at 10.30 am. Tyagvallabh Swami, Dr Swami and Mahant Swami spoke about the importance of guru and the glory of Swamishri. Thereafter Shri Bhupendrasinh Chudasama, Minister for Agriculture, spoke gloriously about Swamishri’s social services and creation of Akshardham in Gandhinagar and New Delhi. Then a leading member of the Congress Party, Shri Shaktisinh Gohil, addressed the assembly.The senior sadhus garlanded Swamishri on behalf of everyone. Then 45,000 devotees in the assembly offered flower petals in obeisance to Swamishri. A traditional dance to honour Swamishri, “Guru roon ada kem kariye”, was performed by children and youths of Adas Satsang Mandal.Finally, Swamishri blessed the mammoth gathering, “Firstly, I offer my respects to all of you who have come from distant places in India and abroad to celebrate Guru Purnima for Thakorji’s darshan and to receive the blessings of sadhus. The glory of Guru Purnima goes back to hundreds of thousands of years. Through such festivals our culture and values are consolidated in our souls. One is inspired during festivals. One comes to take the blessings of God and His Sadhu.”“Our spiritual values give happiness in this life and the life hereafter. Our spiritual values include morality, bhakti, truth, compassion, ahimsa and brahmacharya. Guru Punam is celebrated to consolidate these values. God is the guru of all and through the spiritual gurus who have realized God one receives commands and inspiration. The supreme benefit in this world is to be liberated from the cycles of birth and death, moksha of atma, and attain the eternal bliss of God – one attains this through the guru.”“The government has an ongoing campaign to plant trees for the benefit of our environment. People know that trees give oxygen. Despite knowing this they cut down trees. To survive we need trees. God gives us oxygen free of cost. Plant a few trees every year and then nurture the sapling. This is a great service to society. May God gives us strength to attain our life’s goal of moksha and in performing our worldly duties.”Swamishri announced that all devotees pledge to plant a sapling.On the occasion of the Guru Punam festival hundreds of devotees donated blood at the BAPS blood donation camp organized by the Sanshta’s health services and many more also availed of a diagnostic camp.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
8 July 2006, Bochasan
Saurabh observed a waterless fast for 56 hours.
9 July 2006, Bochasan
Forty-four devotees pilgrimaged 240 km by foot from Vyara.
10 July 2006, Bochacan
Thirty-six devotees pilgrimaged 240 km by foot from Vyara,
37 youths pilgrimaged 40 km by foot from Mirsapura (since 1976 the youths have been travelling by foot to every Guru Punam celebration),
22 devotees from Samarkha and 8 devotees from the Vadi suburb of Vadodara pilgrimaged by foot to the mandir.
17 July 2006, Bochasan
Six youths and two BAPS sadhus pilgrimaged by foot from Mehalav.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj entered the assembly hall, and teenagers who had come from London sang the line "Jogi joya, jovanu kai na rahyu re lol" (Having seen Jogi, nothing remains to be seen). Swamishri went close to them. When his chair turned towards the throne of the hall, Swamishri bent his neck round and, addressing the teenagers sitting behind, said, "Now that nothing remains to be seen, when you go back there, do not watch plays and shows or cinema. When you go there, see only Yogiji Maharaj. Take these provisions with you and remember them."

ds.t: A wonderful provision for the journey
w: Swamishri entered the assembly hall, and teenagers from London sang the line 'Jogi joya, jovanu kai na rahyu re lol' (We have seen Jogi, nothing is left to see). Swamishri came near them. As his chair turned towards the hall's throne, Swamishri bent his neck back and, addressing the teenagers sitting behind, said, "Now if nothing is left to see, then when you go back there, do not watch plays, shows or cinema. There, see only Yogiji Maharaj. Take this provision with you and remember it."

In the evening Swamishri attended the Sunday Satsang assembly. Children of Delhi Bal Mandal presented a cultural programme in which they enacted the stories of Shravan and Nachiketa. Finally they performed a cultural dance. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly in Hindi and Gujarati. He elaborated upon the divine power of Yogiji Maharaj’s wishes and how Satsang flourished in India and abroad. Swamishri also explained the stories of Nachiketa and King Janak and stressed their steadfastness and devotion.

The owner of a mobile phone company called Wincon came for darshan. His two sons were also with him. When Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a box of prasad to the little child, the little one immediately said, "Give it to my elder brother first."
Swamishri was very pleased to see this feeling and said to him, "Your feeling is very good. So God will give you more."

During the meetings, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said to the sons of a devotee, "We know about his nature, but we are not to look at that nature. You, your wives and your children, all of you should serve your father, and do so always."

Dr Mahendrabhai and his two brothers, Madhusudanbhai and Bharatbhai, had come from the USA for darshan. Madhusudanbhai's only son, Akshar, had passed away untimely in his youth, but the firmness that he and his family had kept with matchless conviction was an inspiration to satsangis and to everyone. Madhusudanbhai was meeting Pramukh Swami Maharaj for the first time since Akshar had gone to Akshardham. As soon as he came before Swamishri, he said with strength, "One whose guru is Akshar, he makes him aksharrup and takes him to Akshardham."
Swamishri said, "Akshar has certainly taken his seat in Akshardham."

Today, after finishing his puja, Mahant Swami Maharaj came to his room to take his medicine. Here he laughed and said, "Today, if Nilkanth Swami (Thakorji's attendant) had not come, the puja would have gone on for an hour!"
Then, telling the secret of it, he said, "I was completely lost in the incident about Yogi Bapa."

Among the incidents presented during the puja today, the incident "Swamishri was ill and Yogi Bapa massaged his legs" had been narrated. And after that the kirtan "Haiya na het na bhulay, Yogi tara haiya na het na bhulay..." (the love of your heart cannot be forgotten, O Yogi) had been sung. Swamishri was referring to this.
Swamishri said, "I was not even aware whether I was in puja or not."
How absorbed Swamishri must have been in the memory of his guru!

Today a doormat was shown to Mahant Swami Maharaj, underneath which the teenagers had written their names and the fault that troubles them. And they had requested Swamishri, "Please step on this doormat and crush our faults."
Hearing this, Swamishri immediately said no, no, no, and bowed to the doormat. As if to say, how can one trample with one's feet a doormat on which devotees' names are written?!
On leaving, Swamishri again bowed to the doormat and touched his hand to his head.
What respect and what reverence even for the names of devotees!
In the evening Mahant Swami Maharaj began his walk, along with listening to the book Yogi Vani.
In it came the talk: "One who conducts worldly affairs after asking is free of desires."

Swamishri laughed and said, "He asks in such a way that one has to say yes. There are three types of gopis, aren't there! Among them, the mature one is the very best. In the same way, there are types of devotees too."

Next in the reading came that, having had Vachanamrut Gadhada II 53 read, Yogi Bapa said, "What is the divine understanding of Bhagwan and the sadhu? Not to see the faults of souls but to liberate them."
Swamishri said, "That is why we gain. Otherwise it would be kick out."

In one talk it came: "A devotee of Bhagwan does not desire the four kinds of liberation but desires seva. What is that seva? To hold Bhagwan constantly in the mind and to see as faultless those connected with him."
Swamishri said, "Both are hard, but if one is there, the other happens automatically."
Gnanpriyadas Swami asked, "Here the talk mentions those connected with him; what does connected mean? Those who have taken the vartman (initiation vows)?"
Swamishri said, "Even one who takes the name Swaminarayan once a year is connected."
The sadhus asked in surprise, "But what if a person opposed to satsang says the name Swaminarayan?"
Swamishri said, "Cross him out. It is about one who says it with love and with a sense of glory."

ds.t: Faults do not fly away like that
w: After finishing his evening meal, Mahant Swami Maharaj sang the chesta with the sadhus. Today in the teenagers' assembly there had been a game of releasing balloons. To get a special memory with Swamishri, the sadhus had brought such balloons here, with the names of various faults of nature written on them. The sadhus began releasing these balloons into the air, saying, "In this way we want to make our faults fly away."
Swamishri said, "Faults of nature do not go like that."
The attendant sadhu asked, "Then how do they go?"
"One has to strive," Swamishri answered.
Without any flattery, Swamishri spoke the truth as a true well wisher.

Even when the temperature in Mahant Swami Maharaj's room is 27 degrees, he wears a shawl and a cap. Today a new cap had come for Swamishri. The attendant sadhu gave it to Swamishri to wear. Swamishri said no.
The attendant sadhu said, "It is just like the one you wear."
Pointing to the old cap, Swamishri said, "There is this one!"
The attendant sadhu said, "But use this new one; it too will become loose like that one."
The attendant sadhu was saying this because Swamishri likes to wear a loose, wide cap when sleeping.
Swamishri said, "Just let one stay loose!"
Everyone laughed.
Finally, to persuade Swamishri, the attendant sadhu said, "If you wear the new one, this one can go for washing."
Swamishri said with a straight face, "Wash it tomorrow."
Everyone laughed again.
Swamishri never economises on being economical.
